subject: Re: Competitive pricing request & vendor replacement options
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@helixtech.io>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive pricing compare and potential vendor move

Hi Mateo,

We’re evaluating a potential move off our incumbent inference vendor (sustained token volumes, heavy real-time use, KV cache reliance). Before we go any further we need a side-by-side economics and operational comparison to present to our procurement and infra teams.

Key asks:
- A simple comparison (hosted vs dedicated) that shows net monthly spend at our run-rate (approx 120M tokens/mo + 60M embeddings/mo).
- An alternative commercial option that helps us bridge onboarding risk (short pilot credits or retainer + volume rebate constructs).
- Any estimated ops friction for migrating stateful caches and runtime adapters (KV cache warm-up, custom kernels, peak SLA exposure).

I attached our inference profile that outlines typical sequence lengths, concurrency patterns and SLOs (helixtech_inference-profile.xlsx).

Timing: procurement meeting 8/6. Can you get an initial sketch by next week?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
HelixTech

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@helixtech.io>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive pricing compare and potential vendor move

Sanjay,

Appreciate the data and the clear asks. High-level we can run two pragmatic commercial paths that tend to map to the risk profiles you described:

1) Retainer-first (Dedicated)
- Reserved capacity (dedicated GPU pool) with a small upfront retainer to guarantee spot capacity and predictable latency.
- Add-on: staged onboarding credit to offset the first 60 days of peak egress/cold-cache costs.
- Upside: predictable per-token economics once warmed; straightforward SLA.
- Downside: higher baseline commit.

2) Volume-rebate (Hosted + tiered rebate)
- No large retainer; progressive volume tiers with increasing per-token rebate as you hit commit windows.
- Add-on: short-term pilot credits + automatic fallback to a runtime-compatible quantized variant if you need fast capacity.
- Upside: lower initial commitment.
- Downside: potential latency variability at peaks without dedicated capacity.

Operational notes:
- KV cache migration is the most time-consuming piece; we recommend a staged warm-up plan and a prefix-caching approach to reduce cold-start token costs. Our CS team can estimate warm-up egress and duration after a short profiling run.
- We should include a 30-day rollback credit if the migration materially impacts your SLA during the pilot window.

Attached is an initial sketch (initial-econ-sketch.pdf) with a quick cost delta and two anchoring offers.

Next steps:
- I'll loop in our customer success and pricing lead to refine numbers against your profile.
- If that sounds good, could we schedule a 30-min call Thurs 07/30 to align on which commercial path you prefer?

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive pricing compare and potential vendor move

Mateo / team,

Quick internal notes to sharpen the sketch before the Thurs call.

Operational friction estimates (very rough):
- KV cache warm-up: 20 to 40 business days for a seeded prefix approach (depends on cache size and ability to precompute embeddings).
- Runtime adapter work (kernels/quantization): 10 to 30 weeks for an engineering integration track if they need custom ops; often avoided by using our quantized compatible build.
- Onboarding CS hours: ~800 hours for golden-path migration (comms, handoffs, playbooks).

Commercial levers to reduce risk:
- Short-term bridging credit: we can offer a 30-day $Xk credit to offset cold-cache egress (we'll fill $X after profiling).
- Staged seats: A small retainer for critical latency routes + hosted fallback for burst traffic; simplifies rollback.

I've sketched two concrete dollarized scenarios in the attached internal note (we'll paste the numbers into the call).

Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mateo / Kimberly,

This is helpful and aligns with what procurement was hoping to see. A few clarifying points before the 7/30 call:
- Procurement prefers a lower upfront commitment. The volume-rebate approach is attractive if we can get a firm first-90-day cap on exposure and an explicit rollback credit (we're proposing 25% of three months gross if SLA breach during pilot).
- Security/compliance: can you share the high-level SOC2 artifacts or a link to the security questionnaire? Elaine will handle that track.
- Please put together a short line-item term sheet we can present (cost by tier, pilot credit amount, rollback credit, onboarding hours).

We'd like the call on 07/30 at 11:00 PT. If the term sheet looks reasonable we'll push to a pilot start the week of 8/9.

Sanjay
